title: Red Harbor
tagline: Earth to a home on Mars, with nothing but real engineering.
summary: No warp, no aliens. A small crew of AI units and one human commander build a ship in Earth orbit, cross to Mars on engines we could build, and spend two years finding the place to stay.

layers.name: Leaving the cradle
layers.intro: Everything starts with getting off the ground. Then the ship has to be built where nothing falls.

steps.name: Kármán line
steps.beat: The edge of space. The sky goes black.
steps.fact: The usual line where space begins, 100 km up.

steps.name: ISS orbit
steps.beat: Dock with the station and pick up your first AI unit.
steps.fact: The ISS moves at about 7.7 km/s.

steps.name: Hubble Space Telescope
steps.beat: A service call for the old telescope pays for the next launch.
steps.fact: Hubble has orbited Earth since 1990.

steps.name: Inner Van Allen belt
steps.beat: Radiation spikes. Shield the electronics or lose them.
steps.fact: A ring of trapped protons from about 1,000 to 6,000 km up.

steps.name: GPS constellation
steps.beat: The navigation satellites everyone on Earth relies on.
steps.fact: GPS satellites orbit twice a day at 20,200 km.

steps.name: Outer Van Allen belt
steps.beat: Electrons this time. The Science AI starts mapping the storm.
steps.fact: Trapped electrons, roughly 13,000 to 60,000 km up.

steps.name: Geostationary belt
steps.beat: The shipyard goes here, above one spot on Earth.
steps.fact: Satellites here orbit once a day and seem to hang still.

steps.name: Moon
steps.beat: First crew around the Moon in decades. The ship needs its water.
steps.fact: Apollo crews took about three days to get here.

steps.name: Shackleton crater
steps.beat: Ice in permanent shadow. Fuel and air for Mars.
steps.fact: Its floor at the lunar south pole never sees sunlight.

steps.name: Earth–Moon L2
steps.beat: The Mars ship takes shape behind the Moon.
steps.fact: A balance point about 61,500 km beyond the Moon.

steps.name: Sun–Earth L1
steps.beat: A shakedown flight to the solar observatories.
steps.fact: Solar observatories like SOHO watch the Sun from here.

steps.name: Kamo'oalewa
steps.beat: A test run to Earth's little companion. The ship is ready. The window to Mars opens.
steps.fact: A small asteroid that circles the Sun near Earth; it may be a piece of the Moon.

layers.name: The crossing
layers.intro: The launch window opens once every 26 months. Miss it and you wait. You don't miss it.

steps.name: Apophis
steps.beat: The asteroid that once scared everyone. A good place to test the drill.
steps.fact: It will pass closer than geostationary satellites in April 2029.

steps.name: Bennu
steps.beat: A rubble pile. The surface is so loose the sampler sinks in.
steps.fact: OSIRIS-REx brought a sample of Bennu to Earth in 2023.

steps.name: Ryugu
steps.beat: Carbon and water locked in rock: fuel for later.
steps.fact: Hayabusa2 returned samples of Ryugu in 2020.

steps.name: Didymos and Dimorphos
steps.beat: You pass the moonlet humans once pushed off course.
steps.fact: NASA's DART changed Dimorphos's orbit in 2022.

steps.name: Itokawa
steps.beat: A peanut-shaped asteroid. Two rubble piles stuck together.
steps.fact: The first asteroid sampled and returned, by Hayabusa in 2010.

steps.name: Phaethon
steps.beat: The rock that feeds the Geminid meteors. Its trail pings your shields.
steps.fact: Parent body of the Geminid meteor shower.

steps.name: Unnamed rubble-pile asteroid
steps.beat: No name, no catalogue entry. You name it after your first crew member.
steps.fact: Most near-Earth asteroids smaller than 100 m are still undiscovered.

steps.name: Eros
steps.beat: A big, old rock. NEAR Shoemaker is still sitting on it.
steps.fact: NEAR Shoemaker landed on Eros in 2001.

steps.name: Ganymed
steps.beat: The largest near-Earth asteroid. Enough metal for a city.
steps.fact: About 35 km across, the biggest near-Earth asteroid.

steps.name: Solar storm
steps.beat: A storm from the Sun. Everyone hides in the water-shielded core for three days.
steps.fact: Coronal mass ejections cross the inner Solar System many times a year.

steps.name: Unnamed Mars-crossing asteroid
steps.beat: A last mining stop before Mars.
steps.fact: Thousands of asteroids cross Mars's orbit; many are uncatalogued.

steps.name: Mars sphere of influence
steps.beat: Mars's gravity takes over. Ahead, a red disc grows every hour.
steps.fact: Mars dominates gravity within about 577,000 km.

layers.name: Arrival
layers.intro: Getting to Mars is half the trip. Stopping there is the other half.

steps.name: Deimos
steps.beat: The outer moon. Quiet and dark: a perfect depot.
steps.fact: Deimos is only about 12 km across.

steps.name: Areostationary orbit
steps.beat: Relay satellites go up so the surface can always talk to Earth.
steps.fact: About 17,000 km above Mars, an orbit lasts one Martian day.

steps.name: Phobos
steps.beat: The inner moon is falling toward Mars, slowly. You build a base anyway.
steps.fact: Phobos will break up or crash into Mars in about 50 million years.

steps.name: Stickney crater
steps.beat: The crater that nearly shattered Phobos. Shelter from radiation.
steps.fact: About 9 km wide, on a moon only 22 km across.

steps.name: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter
steps.beat: An old orbiter still taking pictures. Its maps pick your landing sites.
steps.fact: Its HiRISE camera can see objects about a metre across.

steps.name: Mars entry interface
steps.beat: Seven minutes of terror. The heat shield glows.
steps.fact: Landers hit the top of the atmosphere at about 125 km altitude.

steps.name: Jezero Crater
steps.beat: Touchdown in an ancient lake. Perseverance's tracks are still here.
steps.fact: Once a lake with a river delta, now explored by Perseverance.

steps.name: Isidis Planitia
steps.beat: Beagle 2 lies here, solar panels half open. You finish its mission.
steps.fact: Beagle 2 landed here in 2003; it was found in 2015.

steps.name: Gale Crater
steps.beat: Curiosity's mountain, layer after layer of Mars's history.
steps.fact: Curiosity has been climbing Mount Sharp since 2014.

steps.name: Elysium Planitia
steps.beat: InSight felt marsquakes here. You feel one too.
steps.fact: InSight recorded over 1,300 marsquakes.

steps.name: Gusev Crater
steps.beat: Spirit's last stand, stuck in the sand.
steps.fact: The rover Spirit explored Gusev from 2004 to 2010.

steps.name: Meridiani Planum
steps.beat: Opportunity's grave, 45 km from where it landed. You leave a note.
steps.fact: Opportunity drove more than a marathon here.

layers.name: The great features
layers.intro: The biggest volcano, the deepest canyon, the widest basin in the Solar System. You go to see them all.

steps.name: Valles Marineris
steps.beat: A canyon as long as the United States is wide.
steps.fact: About 4,000 km long and up to 7 km deep.

steps.name: Noctis Labyrinthus
steps.beat: A maze of canyons. Mist forms at dawn.
steps.fact: A tangle of steep valleys at the west end of Valles Marineris.

steps.name: Arsia Mons
steps.beat: Dark holes in its flank: lava-tube skylights. A roof against radiation.
steps.fact: Skylight pits on its slopes may lead into caves.

steps.name: Pavonis Mons
steps.beat: On the equator, perfect for a future space elevator.
steps.fact: Sits almost exactly on the Martian equator.

steps.name: Ascraeus Mons
steps.beat: Tallest of the three Tharsis giants.
steps.fact: Rises about 18 km above the surrounding plain.

steps.name: Olympus Mons
steps.beat: The summit is above most of the atmosphere. Stars at noon.
steps.fact: About 22 km high, the tallest volcano known.

steps.name: Tempe Terra
steps.beat: Old cracked crust. Ice hides in the shadows.
steps.fact: An ancient highland split by faults.

steps.name: Chryse Planitia
steps.beat: Viking 1 still stands here, facing the sunset it photographed.
steps.fact: Viking 1 landed here in 1976.

steps.name: Ares Vallis
steps.beat: An old flood channel. Sojourner's tiny tracks.
steps.fact: Mars Pathfinder and Sojourner landed here in 1997.

steps.name: Cydonia
steps.beat: The 'face' turns out to be a hill. The crew laughs for the first time in weeks.
steps.fact: Home of the famous 'Face on Mars', a mesa seen in 1976.

steps.name: Utopia Planitia
steps.beat: Buried ice the size of a lake. Water for a town.
steps.fact: Radar found a buried ice deposit as big as Lake Superior.

steps.name: Hellas Planitia
steps.beat: The deepest basin. The air is thickest here, almost enough for liquid water.
steps.fact: About 7 km deep and 2,300 km across.

layers.name: Water and shelter
layers.intro: A home needs water, shelter from radiation and something to build with. The search narrows.

steps.name: Argyre Planitia
steps.beat: Old glaciers may lie under the dust here.
steps.fact: A giant impact basin in the southern highlands.

steps.name: Holden crater
steps.beat: Lakebeds stacked like pages.
steps.fact: Its floor holds layered sediments from an ancient lake.

steps.name: Eberswalde delta
steps.beat: A river once flowed here and dropped its mud in a fan.
steps.fact: One of the clearest ancient river deltas on Mars.

steps.name: Mawrth Vallis
steps.beat: Clay layers. Water sat here for a long time.
steps.fact: One of the richest clay deposits on Mars.

steps.name: Arabia Terra
steps.beat: Some of the oldest ground on Mars.
steps.fact: Possibly the oldest terrain on the planet.

steps.name: Deuteronilus Mensae
steps.beat: Glaciers under rubble, flowing a centimetre a year.
steps.fact: Radar shows ice-rich glaciers buried under debris.

steps.name: Protonilus Mensae
steps.beat: More buried ice, closer to the surface.
steps.fact: Mesas with debris-covered glaciers between them.

steps.name: Phlegra Montes
steps.beat: Ice at mid-latitudes, where the sun still warms the panels.
steps.fact: Ice-rich ground shallow enough to dig.

steps.name: Arcadia Planitia
steps.beat: Ice a few metres down and flat ground. Your top candidate.
steps.fact: A favourite candidate landing region for human missions, for its shallow ice.

steps.name: Korolev crater
steps.beat: A crater filled with ice, 1.8 km thick.
steps.fact: Holds about 2,200 cubic kilometres of water ice.

steps.name: Vastitas Borealis
steps.beat: The northern lowlands. Perhaps an ocean once.
steps.fact: Some scientists think an ocean filled these lowlands.

steps.name: Planum Boreum
steps.beat: The north pole: layered ice holding millions of years of climate.
steps.fact: The north polar cap is about 3 km thick.

layers.name: Red Harbor
layers.intro: Two years from Earth. Time to choose where humanity stays.

steps.name: Chasma Boreale
steps.beat: A canyon cut into the polar cap itself.
steps.fact: A valley about 500 km long in the north polar ice.

steps.name: Olympia Undae
steps.beat: Gypsum dunes. Water once evaporated here.
steps.fact: The largest dune field on Mars, rich in gypsum.

steps.name: Medusae Fossae
steps.beat: Soft rock carved by wind. Maybe ice inside.
steps.fact: Radar suggests it may hold enough ice to cover Mars 1.5 m deep.

steps.name: Nili Fossae
steps.beat: Methane traces. Something, someday, made gas here.
steps.fact: Rich in clays and carbonates; methane was reported nearby.

steps.name: Syrtis Major
steps.beat: The dark patch seen from Earth by the first telescopes.
steps.fact: The first Martian feature mapped from Earth, in 1659.

steps.name: Hesperia Planum
steps.beat: Old lava plains that set the clock for Mars's history.
steps.fact: It names a whole era of Martian geology, the Hesperian.

steps.name: Promethei Terra
steps.beat: Lobate debris aprons. Ice under every slope.
steps.fact: Its craters hold debris-covered glaciers.

steps.name: Planum Australe
steps.beat: The south cap, frozen carbon dioxide over water ice.
steps.fact: Its water ice could cover Mars about 11 m deep.

steps.name: Subglacial lake candidate
steps.beat: A bright radar echo under the ice. You drill. The answer is complicated.
steps.fact: A 2018 radar signal hinted at liquid water under the south cap; it's still debated.

steps.name: Lava tube cave
steps.beat: A tube big enough for a town, roofed in rock. The radiation drops to Earth levels.
steps.fact: Mars has many skylight pits; lava tubes like Earth's are expected beneath them.

steps.name: Pavonis cave entrance
steps.beat: The first permanent airlock goes in.
steps.fact: Pit chains on Tharsis volcanoes are likely collapsed lava tubes.

steps.name: Red Harbor
steps.beat: Ice nearby, rock overhead, sunlight on the panels. You name the place and send the message home: 'Come.'
steps.fact: Built inside a real-type Martian lava tube near Tharsis.
